title: InKAN: B-Spline KANs via Truncated Power Form
summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) place learnable B-spline activations on network edges rather than fixed activations on nodes. The standard Cox-de Boor recursion evaluates these activations through $k$ sequential passes for degree-$k$ splines, consuming over 90% of forward-pass time. InKAN replaces this recursion with the truncated power form, a classical result from approximation theory that expresses each uniform cubic B-spline as five $(x)_+^3$ terms at shifted knot positions.
